cards.claim: The mole (symbol mol) is the SI unit of amount of substance; one mole contains exactly 6.02214076 × 10^23 elementary entities.
cards.quote: The mole, symbol mol, is the SI unit of amount of substance. One mole contains exactly 6.02214076 × 1023 elementary entities.

cards.claim: Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance in grams; in grams it is numerically equal to the atomic, molecular or formula mass in u.
cards.quote: the mass of one mole of a substance in grams is called its molar mass. The molar mass in grams is numerically equal to atomic/molecular/formula mass in u.

cards.claim: One mole of any kind of entity (atoms, molecules or formula units) contains 6.022 × 10^23 of those entities, e.g. 1 mol of water contains 6.022 × 10^23 water molecules.
cards.quote: 1 mol of hydrogen atoms = 6.022 × 1023 atoms 1 mol of water molecules = 6.022 × 1023 water molecules 1 mol of sodium chloride = 6.022 ×1023 formula units of sodium chloride

cards.claim: The molar volume of a gas at STP depends on the STP convention: 22.4 L per mole at the old STP (273.15 K, 1 atm) and 22.7 L at the new STP (273.15 K, 1 bar).
cards.quote: Old STP conditions 273.15 K, 1 atm, volume occupied by 1 mol of gas = 22.4 L. New STP conditions 273.15 K, 1 bar, volume occupied by a gas = 22.7 L.

cards.claim: NCERT finds the number of atoms in one mole of carbon from the mass of one carbon-12 atom (1.992648 × 10^-23 g, by mass spectrometry) and the mass of one mole of carbon (12 g). The quotient is garbled in the PDF text; the equation gives it.
cards.quote: the mass of a carbon–12 atom was determined by a mass spectrometer and found to be equal to 1.992648 × 10–23 g. Knowing that one mole of carbon weighs 12 g, the number of atoms in it is equal to:

cards.claim: A mole is a count of entities, not a fixed mass: one mole of any substance contains the same number of entities, whatever the substance.
cards.quote: It may be emphasised that the mole of a substance always contains the same number of entities, no matter what the substance may be.

cards.claim: NCERT Exemplar 1.5 (MCQ I): which sample contains the greatest number of atoms: 4 g He, 46 g Na, 0.40 g Ca or 12 g He?
cards.quote: The number of atoms present in one mole of an element is equal to Avogadro number. Which of the following element contains the gr eatest number of atoms? (i) 4g He (ii) 46g Na (iii) 0.40g Ca (iv) 12g He
